summary: 24-year-old man, 24 h migratory RIF pain, anorexia, vomiting, low-grade fever, localised peritonism, WBC 14.8, CRP 48. Clinically uncomplicated appendicitis.

inputs.hpi: 24-hour history of central abdominal pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa overnight. Constant, sharp, 7/10, worse on movement and coughing. Anorexia since yesterday, nausea and two episodes of vomiting. Feels feverish. No diarrhoea, no urinary symptoms, no previous similar episodes.
symptoms: migration of pain to the right iliac fossa

exam.general: Alert, flushed, lying still. Temperature 38.1°C, pulse 102/min, BP 128/78.
exam.abdomen: Tender with voluntary guarding in the right iliac fossa, maximal at McBurney's point. Rebound tenderness in the RIF. Rovsing's sign positive. No palpable mass. Bowel sounds present. Hernial orifices normal.

labs.name: Urine dipstick
labs.resultText: Negative for blood, leucocytes and nitrites

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute appendicitis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute appendicitis — clinically uncomplicated (Alvarado 9, AIR 7). No clinical features of perforation.

emergencyLevel.note: Suspected acute appendicitis needs same-day surgical assessment; in an outpatient practice this is an ER / same-day referral, never a routine booking.

recommended.note: WSES 2020 favours the AIR (or Adult Appendicitis Score) over Alvarado for risk stratification in adults.
recommended.knownGapNote: Web CDS has no AIR rule (and no AIR calculator); Alvarado only.

values.note: Migration 1 + anorexia 1 + nausea/vomiting 1 + RIF tenderness 2 + rebound 1 + temperature ≥37.3 1 + WBC >10 2 = 9 (neutrophils 72%, no left-shift point).
Vomiting 1 + RIF pain 1 + rebound (medium) 2 + temp <38.5 0 + PMN 70–84% 1 + WBC 10–14.9 1 + CRP 10–49 1 = 7 (intermediate, 5–8). Web has no AIR calculator.

The record documents migration, anorexia, vomiting, RIF tenderness and rebound; an auto-filled Alvarado below 7 would show 'unlikely/possible' for a probable appendicitis until the clinician ticks the boxes.
values.knownGapNote: iOS auto-fill reads only temperature and WBC (3/10); history and examination items stay unticked.

mustInclude.note: WSES 2020: imaging (US first; CT when US is non-diagnostic or risk is intermediate) before or alongside the surgical decision.
WSES 2020: laparoscopic appendicectomy is the preferred treatment for uncomplicated acute appendicitis (antibiotic-first is an option in selected patients after shared decision).
WSES 2020: a single pre-operative dose of broad-spectrum antibiotic.

mustExclude.note: WSES 2020: no routine postoperative antibiotics after appendicectomy for uncomplicated appendicitis.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web appendicectomy operative-plan prompt prescribes 5 days of co-amoxiclav after simple appendicitis.

pathway.note: New acute problem, no previous encounters: full history, examination and work-up.

guideline.name: WSES Jerusalem guidelines — diagnosis and treatment of acute appendicitis (2020 update)
guideline.section: Diagnosis (clinical scores; imaging), operative treatment (laparoscopic appendicectomy), antibiotic prophylaxis
guideline.citation: Di Saverio S, Podda M, De Simone B, et al. Diagnosis and treatment of acute appendicitis: 2020 update of the WSES Jerusalem guidelines. World J Emerg Surg. 2020;15:27.

guideline.name: Alvarado score (MANTRELS)
guideline.section: Score items and weights; ≤4 unlikely, 5–6 possible, 7–8 probable, 9–10 very probable
guideline.citation: Alvarado A. A practical score for the early diagnosis of acute appendicitis. Ann Emerg Med. 1986;15:557–64.

guideline.name: Appendicitis Inflammatory Response (AIR) score
guideline.section: Score items and weights; 0–4 low, 5–8 intermediate, 9–12 high
guideline.citation: Andersson M, Andersson RE. The appendicitis inflammatory response score: a tool for the diagnosis of acute appendicitis that outperforms the Alvarado score. World J Surg. 2008;32:1843–9.

rationale: Base case for appendicitis. Every engine should recognise the classic picture, raise at least urgent acuity, recommend the appendicitis scores, calculate them correctly and propose laparoscopic appendicectomy with pre-operative antibiotics.
